title: Type-Safe RPC/REST Client with Path Parameter Inference
businessContext: A microservices ecosystem requires an internal SDK. Frontend engineers frequently write typos in URL routes like `/users/:userId/orders/:orderId` or pass wrong query parameters, resulting in 404s and missing request bodies that only surface in production.
problemStatement: Design a generic TypeScript utility type `ExtractRouteParams<TPath>` that extracts route param names from a template string like `"/orgs/:orgId/repos/:repoId"` into a strongly typed object `{ orgId: string; repoId: string }`. Build a typed client interface ensuring paths and parameters match at compile time.
constraints: Must recursively infer all `:param` tokens from any route string.
Routes without params must yield an empty object or void.
Path and param arguments must be validated at compile time with zero runtime overhead.
candidateTasks: Implement `ExtractRouteParams<T>` using template literal types, conditional types, and recursion.
Handle trailing slashes and multi-param paths.
Ensure the `params` argument is required if parameters exist, and optional if the route has no parameters.
hints: Use conditional types with template literals: `T extends `${infer Start}:${infer Param}/${infer Rest}``. Use recursion on `Rest`.
Make sure single-parameter routes at the end of the string are captured: `T extends `${infer Start}:${infer Param}``.

testCases.name: Resolves path parameters into URL path
testCases.explanation: Path parameters are interpolated into resolved route.

alternativeApproaches: Using OpenAPI generator / tRPC / ts-rest for complete full-stack contract sharing.
commonMistakes: Infinite recursion in type aliases leading to "Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite".
Not supporting optional params when routes have no parameters.
